title: C482/256/2010 of SHRI C.M.JOHRI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 256 of 2010
Shri. C.M. Johari .....Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another ....Respondents
Mr. Shiv Pandey, Advocate on behalf of Mr. Anurag Bisaria, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Deputy Advocate General with Mr. Lalit Miglani, Brief Holder for
the State.
 Dated: 7th December, 2018
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 When this C482 application was entertained by this
Court on 26.03.2010, notices were issued to respondent no. 2, the
complainant. The applicant had taken steps for serving the
respondent No. 2 and there is an office report dated 29.03.2010
that respondent no. 2 has been served personally.
2. Further on 02.08.2013, fresh notices were issued for
the second time to the respondent no. 2, and on the steps being
taken by the applicant, there is an office report dated 24.09.2013
that the registered notices were received back unserved. Hence, yet
again the Court for the third time directed issuance of notice to
respondent no. 2 on 17.05.2014 afresh. The steps were taken for
serving the respondent no. 2 through Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Haridwar. There is an office report dated 16.06.2014 which reads
as under:
"Notices issued to respondent no. 2 received back
unserved because noticee refused to take notice as per the
report of police station Jawalapur".
3. For the fourth time, this Court on 31.07.2018 had
issued notices to the respondent no. 2 for fixing 05.09.2018, on
which, steps were taken on 06.08.2018, by the applicant and it is
reported by the Registry vide its report dated 04.09.2018 that

2
notices issued to respondent no. 2 has been received by him
personally. Meaning thereby, as per the office report, the
respondent no. 2 has been served personally and it would be
deemed that respondent No. 2 has the knowledge of the proceeding
of the Court, but, he has deliberately chosen not to put in
appearance or contest the proceedings.
4. The applicant of the present C482 Application
challenges the summoning order dated 18.08.2008 and the
consequential order dated 24.02.2010 issuing non bailable
warrants in Complaint Case No. 2220 of 2007, Prakash Sharma
Vs. C.M. Johari, which on the date of the admission of C482
application, i.e. 26.03.2010, was pending consideration and has
prayed for quashing the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 2220
of 2007.
5. Considering the submission made by the counsel for
the applicant that as far as the controversy pertaining to the
purchase of coolers from the shop of the complainant/respondent
no. 2 is concerned, on account of the same not functioning the
applicant has lodged a complaint before the Consumer Grievance
Redressal Forum and the complaint thus filed by him before
District Consumer Forum Numbered as 228 of 2007, C.M. Johari
as proprietor M/s Namashkar Electrical has been decided by the
judgment dated 11.09.2008 in favour of the applicant, which is
annexed as Annexure no. 1 to the C482 application. The District
Consumer Redressal Forum had allowed the Complaint Case No.
228 of 2007 with the following finding:

6. The argument of the learned counsel for the applicant
is that the initiation of the present criminal complaint proceedings
as lodged by the complainant/respondent (which was initially
registered as 5822 of 2007) has been assigned with new number as
Complaint Case No. 2220 of 2007 by invoking Section 420 of the
IPC was nothing but a counter blast to the proceedings drawn
before the District Consumer Forum. Because the applicant has
filed the case before the District Consumer Forum on 27.07.2007,
which was decided on 11.09.2008, was registered prior in time and
the complaint was filed by respondent on 05.11.2007, much
thereafter.
7. The basis of complaint as lodged by respondent No. 2
was based on the fact that accused applicant has purchased two
coolers on credit and has not paid the amount despite of promise
made to make the payment within 10 to 12 days. Allegation was
that when despite of demand raised, when the payment was not
made, rather he submitted in the complaint that on 29.10.2007,
some unknown person visited his shop and said that applicant has
informed that he will not make the payment, the complainant can
take back the coolers. Its then only that complainant alleges he
lodged complaint under Sections 420, 323, 504, 506 and 427 I.P.C.
at P.S. Jwalapur, District Haridwar on 05.11.2007.
8. On the other hand, in a proceeding initiated prior in
time before District Consumer Grievance Forum, which was
contested by the complainant, the Forum held that the complainant
at no point of time prior to lodging the complaint had given any
notice of demand of any money due from the applicant, thus, it was
held that in fact no amount was due to be paid by the applicant,

4
rather complainant admitted that he had sold the coolers which was
found to be defective and was never put to use by applicant and it
was lying useless with him which has resulted into loss for him.
When according to the case as established, when the complainant
admits sale, it would only be after exchange of consideration. The
act of not making any demand would rather mean, in fact, that no
amount was due to be paid by the applicant, if that be so, no
offence as alleged in the complaint would be made out against the
applicant.
9. The propriety of the criminal complaint which was
lodged against the present applicant was based on the allegation
due to non payment of alleged price of the coolers, the impact of
the same already stood tested vide judgment 11.09.2008 by the
Courts and thereafter a summoning order was issued against the
present applicant on 18.08.2008 and, consequently, by the
subsequent order dated 24.02.2010, non-bailable warrants were
issued against the applicant. The Court of A.C.J.M. 1st Haridwar
has issued the summoning order on 18.08.2008, which is under
challenge in the present C-482 Application along with the order
dated 24.02.2010 issuing non-bailable warrants.
10. Having gone through the summoning order, this Court
is of the view that considering the impact of the order of Consumer
Grievance Redressal Forum, proceedings which was culminated in
favour of the applicant, as a matter of fact, the allegations raised in
the FIR with regard to the purchase of two coolers along with
accessories on credit would not be tenable because in view of the
finding which has been recorded by the Consumer Grievance
Redressal Forum, it was found that the complainant/respondent
had never issued any notices nor any proceeding was drawn by
him and the Court held that this itself shows that the
complainant/respondent no. 2 was not entitled to receive any
payment from the applicant. Also considering the fact that it
has been held out by the said judgment of the Consumer Grievance

5
Redressal Forum that the coolers, thus purchased, were defective
and were never made operational and remained unutilized, the
proceedings were decided in favour of the applicant and it leads to
an inference that complaint case is as an afterthought as has been
reflected in the complaint which was lodged by the respondent No.
2 against the present applicant.
11. In view of the above, this C-482 Application would
stands allowed and the summoning order dated 18th August, 2008
as well a the Case No. 2220 of 2007, Prakash Sharma Vs. C.M.
Johari, pending before the A.C.J.M. 1st, , Haridwar would too stand
quashed.
12. There would be no order as to costs.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 07.12.2018
Shiv
